lockedMove.speaker: Bart Ehrman
lockedMove.proposition: Churches could have assigned authoritative names to anonymous Gospels when rival named writings emerged, choosing two disciples and two associates of leading apostles as natural legitimating figures.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: four gospels that everybody in the churches, the main church is reading, but they don't have names. And all these heretics are using these other ones saying they're written by apostles. We need authority for these books. We better name them. They named them after authorities. Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. They needed the authority, and so they gave them the names. And they chose fairly natural names. They picked two of Jesus' disciples
